newsitem.title: USA: Implant testimony fails to prove illness link - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Implant testimony fails to prove illness link - WSJ.

text.p: Scientific experts apparently failed to provide compelling evidence linking silicone breast implants to immune-system illnesses, The Wall Street Journal said.

In Friday's electronic edition, the paper said that in an unprecedented court hearing on the science of silicone, plaintiffs' experts testified about a variety of symptoms from fatigue to mental impairment that they had seen in thousand of women with implants.
The experts said they believe the women have developed a new form of immune-system disease, the paper said.
But their audience, a panel of four doctors, viewed this and other testimony as uncompelling, the paper said.

"At some point you're going to have to find a silicone-specific (blood test), or there will always be questions" about whether a link truly exists, one of the panellists told doctors representing the plaintiffs, the paper said.
The panellists will serve as court-appointed experts in potentially thousands of future silicone cases, the paper said.
